turns.en: If I had not done this ridiculous thing in my portfolio, I wouldn't have this crazy app. Some of the ideas I had early in my career, I look at them, I'm like, oh man, never would have been built. So difficult to do it. And now I look at them, I'm like, I can build that now. It's just insane. Welcome to Dive Club. My name is Rid and this is where designers never stop learning. This week's episode is with Tom Johnson from Vercel, who just released one of the coolest personal sites that I have ever seen. And so he's going to give us a little behind the scenes of his process, which sparks a lot of questions about what does it really mean to be a designer today. But before we do a deep dive into this question of identity, let's have a look at Tom's new portfolio.
turns.zh: 如果我没有在作品集里做这件荒唐的事，就不会有这个疯狂的应用。我职业生涯早期的一些想法，现在回头看，我会想，天哪，那些想法永远不可能被实现，太难了。而现在我看着它们，我会想，我现在能把它做出来。这太疯狂了。欢迎来到 Dive Club。我是 Rid，这里是设计师永不停止学习的地方。本周的嘉宾是来自 Vercel 的 Tom Johnson，他刚刚发布了我见过的最酷的个人网站之一。所以他将给我们讲讲他过程的一些幕后故事，这会引发很多关于当今设计师真正意味着什么的问题。但在我们深入探讨这个身份问题之前，让我们先看看 Tom 的新作品集。

turns.en: I've never liked my design portfolio. I've never liked the fixation on portfolios. I've never really liked the discussion around portfolios. It's weird that I'm now talking about the portfolio, but it was more like I just wanted something where I could just do whatever I wanted to and have no limits on it because I feel like when I have seen the best portfolios, they are true representations of the designer behind them. Like I can see their personality and then when I work with them or you know we're actually chatting, I can be like, "Oh yeah, that clicks. That that's that person." And so I was kind of hiding behind the very basic, very minimal, mysterious kind of like wall of logos portfolio for a while.
turns.zh: 我从来不喜欢我的设计作品集。我从来不喜欢对作品集的执念。我从来不太喜欢关于作品集的讨论。很奇怪我现在在谈论作品集，但更多的是我只是想要一个我可以随心所欲、没有限制的东西，因为我觉得当我看到最好的作品集时，它们是背后设计师的真实呈现。就像我能看到他们的个性，然后当我与他们合作或者我们真正聊天时，我可以觉得，“哦对，这就对上了。那就是那个人。”所以有一段时间，我有点躲在非常基础、非常简约、神秘的那种 logo 墙作品集后面。

turns.en: Those are fine. like it's not a bad deal, but it's just it wasn't it wasn't really fun. It wasn't really like what I wanted to to showcase and I knew that I had an opportunity to make something and it had been sitting in my back burner for like a year. I I kept coming back to an old version of it and I just couldn't hit publish cuz it was marginally better and it was just why would I move off of the one that was working? I needed to have a good reason for it. So the the motivation was entirely like just do something fun. It was also something that what I I've had people reach out to me and ask me for portfolio reviews in the past. And the thing I've told them is just like show your personality. Make it a playground. Make it about like something that you isn't just like a wall of cards with your work on it. Like I want to see the the person behind the work, not necessarily just the work. I needed to take my own advice there.
turns.zh: 那些作品集没问题，不是坏事，但就是不太有趣。那并不是我想展示的东西，我知道我有机会做一些东西，它已经在我脑后搁置了一年。我不断回到一个旧版本，但我就是无法点击发布，因为它只是稍微好一点，我为什么要离开那个已经能用的版本？我需要一个充分的理由。所以动机完全就是做点有趣的事。另外，过去有人联系我，请我点评作品集。我告诉他们的就是展示你的个性。把它变成一个游乐场。让它成为某种东西，而不是仅仅一墙卡片展示你的作品。我想看到作品背后的人，而不仅仅是作品。我需要接受自己的建议。

turns.en: I'm sure the tour like the actual tour of this portfolio is probably, you know, 20 minutes long in itself cuz I've played with this. It's unbelievable how deep it is and how many different directions you can go. But orient us a little bit. talk a little bit about, you know, what did you make and then maybe we can kind of dig into like how the vision for it even evolved and and what it actually takes to bring something like this to life.
turns.zh: 我确信这个作品集的导览本身可能就有 20 分钟长，因为我玩过这个。它有多深、你能走多少个不同方向，真是难以置信。但给我们大致介绍一下。谈谈你做了什么，然后也许我们可以深入探讨这个愿景是如何演变的，以及真正把这样的东西做出来需要什么。

turns.en: Literally what I made was I made a game and I needed characters in the game and it definitely didn't start as a game. It just kind of like evented ended up as a game but I made it so like you know what what do you put in the game? You need to have assets. You need to have things that make sense. You need to have 3D objects. And so it was just kind of like if there's a world then I'll populate it with things that are memorable. And yeah, and it was just kind of like me realizing I can make these buildings whatever I want. If I got videos of myself, let's make a movie theater. Let's choose a movie theater that I used to drive by all the time when I was in Milwaukee.
turns.zh: 实际上我做的是一个游戏，我需要游戏里的角色，但它绝对不是一开始就是游戏。它只是最终变成了游戏，但我做了它，所以你知道，你在游戏里放什么？你需要有资产。你需要有合理的东西。你需要有 3D 物体。所以就像是，如果有一个世界，那我就用令人难忘的东西填充它。是的，就是我意识到我可以把这些建筑做成我想要的任何样子。如果我有自己的视频，那就做个电影院吧。选一个我在密尔沃基时经常开车经过的电影院。

turns.en: Real quick message and then we can jump back into it. The team at Paper has been shipping like crazy recently. I mean everything from rich text editing to paper mono to file management through the MCP and their founder Steven just teased their take on components which I think is going to create a whole new precedent in design tooling and paper has really quickly went from being the new kid on the block to the design tool of choice for people shipping with agents. So, if you're still somehow on the sidelines, head to dive.club/paper. And I think you're pretty quickly going to realize why so many designers are making the switch. I've been doing a lot of building right from my phone recently. So, the new Framer MCP is a huge unlock. And say I want to make some updates to the dive club CMS. All I have to do is drop a voice note to Claude or Grok Bot and I can make any change that I want on the go. So, I get all of the benefits of Framer for exploring ideas on the canvas, nailing down responsive design, updating my CMS, but now everything that I could do in Framer, my agents can do for me. It's a big deal and another reason why I'm all in on Framer for the Dive website. So, head to dive.comclub/framer to connect your agent today. Now, on to the episode.
turns.zh: 快速说一条消息，然后我们继续。Paper 团队最近一直在疯狂发布新功能。我是说从富文本编辑到 paper mono 再到通过 MCP 进行文件管理，他们的创始人 Steven 刚刚预告了他们对组件的诠释，我认为这将在设计工具领域创造全新的先例，Paper 真的很快从新秀变成了用智能体发布产品的人的首选设计工具。所以，如果你还在观望，请访问 dive.club/paper。我想你很快会明白为什么这么多设计师在转向它。我最近经常直接从手机上进行构建。所以，新的 Framer MCP 是一个巨大的突破。比如说我想对 Dive Club 的 CMS 做一些更新。我所要做的就是给 Claude 或 Grok Bot 发一条语音笔记，我就可以在移动中做任何我想做的更改。所以，我获得了 Framer 的所有好处：在画布上探索想法、确定响应式设计、更新我的 CMS，但现在我可以在 Framer 中做的一切，我的智能体都可以为我做。这很重要，也是我全力选择 Framer 做 Dive 网站的另一个原因。所以，请访问 dive.comclub/framer 今天连接你的智能体。现在，回到节目。

turns.en: One thing led to another and I realized like there was no limitations behind like what I could show. That's where it landed. But it didn't start as a game. I can't stress that enough. Like it literally did not start as a game. I wasn't like let's make a game with my face in it. It was not this.
turns.zh: 一件事导致另一件事，我意识到我可以展示的东西没有限制。这就是它最终的样子。但它不是一开始就是游戏。我怎么强调都不为过。它真的不是一开始就是游戏。我不是说“让我们做个有我脸的游戏”。不是这样的。

turns.en: Where did it start then?
turns.zh: 那它是从哪里开始的？

turns.en: Yeah. So I actually have a case study in here. I added this a couple days ago because I realized this is a really interesting project and I didn't write much in here. So this is where it started. I had this version of a site and I was like, "Oh, cool. I'll just make the cards dragable and like you can expand them." And I was using dial kit for the first time and I was like, "Oh, let's put the dial kit on the page and people can change the the easings." And it was basically just the same site I had before. I didn't love that. And so I then I tried this and I was just kind of this like what if everything radiates from the middle and you can zoom out and spin things. And I showed it to my wife and she's like why? This is not that interesting. And I was like you're right it's not that interesting. And it also didn't scale at all. So if I had like a lot of projects like how do I show those in a small circle? I didn't like it. And then I was working on this game and this pilgrimage game. I've been working on 3JS a lot and I was like, well, the best way to show that game would be to bring in the assets. So, what if I made this also isometric. So then I I designed this version, which was basically just like a dark isometric space with my truck and camper on it. That was the first thing I built with the idea of like, I'll bring in the game assets from the game and show them there. And oh, I'll make the truck drivable and I'll make it so you can hook up the camper and stuff. And then I started going into like, well, what if I could lower the bunk beds and put out the slides and all this like kind of gamey stuff cuz I was kind of in the mind space. And then I basically then said, well, you maybe it should be a town, if it's a camper, it should be in the woods.
turns.zh: 是的。所以我实际上在这里有一个案例研究。我几天前添加了这个，因为我意识到这是一个非常有趣的项目，我在这里写得不多。所以这就是它的起点。我有这个版本的网站，我当时想，“哦，酷。我就让卡片可拖动，并且可以展开。”我当时第一次使用 dial kit，我想，“哦，让我们把 dial kit 放在页面上，人们可以改变缓动效果。”它基本上就是我之前那个网站。我不喜欢那样。然后我尝试了这个，就是这种“如果一切都从中间辐射出来，你可以缩小并旋转东西”的想法。我给我妻子看了，她说为什么？这没那么有趣。我说你说得对，这没那么有趣。而且它根本不能扩展。所以如果我有很多项目，我怎么在一个小圆圈里展示它们？我不喜欢它。然后我在做这个游戏和这个朝圣游戏。我一直在大量使用 3JS，我想，展示那个游戏的最好方式就是把资产带进来。所以，如果我也把这个做成等距视角呢？然后我设计了这个版本，基本上就是一个黑暗的等距空间，上面有我的卡车和露营车。那是我构建的第一件东西，想法是，我会把游戏中的资产带进来并展示在那里。哦，我会让卡车可驾驶，我会让你可以连接露营车等等。然后我开始想，如果我能放下双层床、推出滑梯，所有这些游戏化的东西，因为我在那种思维空间里。然后我基本上说，也许它应该是一个小镇，如果是露营车，它应该在树林里。

turns.en: And then you can kind of see the natural evolution of things. I had that selected work was just building with cards on the side. I'm like, why would I make a library? So I'll use a library that was near where I used to live in Nashville that won a bunch of awards. So I'm like, okay, this is a library that I'll pull in and make the Ditherface a ridiculous gallery that plays classical music when you walk in and you wear a tuxedo and stuff like that. And then now it's this version here that I have that you are able to walk around in. And I have my bike. That's the bike I have outside. You can ride it and it makes it easier to get around and stuff. And it's just ridiculous.
turns.zh: 然后你可以看到事物的自然演变。我那个精选作品部分原本只是在旁边用卡片搭建的。我想，为什么要做一个图书馆呢？所以我就用了一个我以前住在纳什维尔时附近的图书馆，它得过很多奖。所以我想，好吧，这是一个图书馆，我要把它拉进来，把 Ditherface 做成一个荒谬的画廊，当你走进去时会播放古典音乐，你穿着燕尾服之类的。然后现在就是我有的这个版本，你可以四处走动。我还有我的自行车。那就是我外面的自行车。你可以骑它，它让出行更容易之类的。这太荒谬了。

turns.en: So cool.
turns.zh: 太酷了。

turns.en: Even you can even jump up. But like there's all these game controls and stuff like that in there. And then I spent way too much time trying to figure out like how do you navigate the space? That was the most difficult problem. Is the visitor the character or are they me or are they controlling me or is this a game or are they navigating it or how do they navigate it? And how do also do you navigate it without it feeling like it's slow? Like if I made this with a character you have to like walk around to visit everything. It felt really slow.
turns.zh: 你甚至可以跳起来。但那里有所有这些游戏控制之类的。然后我花了太多时间试图弄清楚你怎么在这个空间里导航？那是最困难的问题。访客是那个角色，还是他们是我，还是他们在控制我，或者这是一个游戏，还是他们在导航，他们如何导航？还有你如何导航它而不让它感觉缓慢？比如，如果我用一个角色来做这个，你必须走来走去才能参观所有东西。那感觉真的很慢。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And that was very gamey. Like okay if I'm looking at like a RTS or something like that or like a game where you would actually have to explore, no one's doing that. So I had to make it so that you could break away from the character and move around and click like you would on a website. And then the character would try to play catchup like if you notice over here
turns.zh: 那非常游戏化。就像好吧，如果我在看一个 RTS 之类的，或者一个你实际上必须探索的游戏，没人会那样做。所以我必须让你能够脱离角色，像在网站上一样四处移动和点击。然后角色会试图追赶，就像你注意到这里

turns.en: I'm running I'm running over because I knew like as soon as I did that then it was like I'm still controlling the character but I'm kind of telling him where to go and he's like playing catchup and that was fun. So it made the site feel a lot less slow and then there was also the issues of like do I click and drag? What are the controls for navigating 3D space? You know, do I zoom? I had those inverted for a while. like can I rotate the screen? Is it free form? Is it first person? Is it third person? It made me appreciate game designers quite a bit because there's so much that is not intuitive from a from a flat interface designer. There's so much more that I had to do around navigating a 3D space. Like if you're looking at the back wall of a building, like if you rotate the camera R for rotate, I show the back walls of the buildings. But if then I if I had the front wall and there's a doorway in it, then you can't see the doorway. So I have to show the doorway a little bit so you know how to exit the building. have to have these like accented highlights on a hover so you know what's clickable because not everything is clickable. So I have this like ghosted effect that shows up with the the chip so you know what you're clicking and it's like all these different product design adjacent problems that I would have solved elsewhere but it was so much different in the 3D space. Do I make it so you know how to climb the the ladder or do I make it so you can just click up there and he knows to navigate up the twisty ladder? Like those are weird problems because if I'm in third person, which I spin this around, love this interaction. If I spin this around, you can still now navigate into that space there. And that's the same tile that I had or but now in the different camera viewport, I have to navigate you separately. And it's just like a weird thing where like now I have to spin the camera around. If you're moving in a certain direction for a certain amount of time, like I have to spin it around. It's a lot. It's a lot. And I've seen other people.
turns.zh: 我跑，我跑过来是因为我知道一旦我那样做，就像我仍然在控制角色，但我有点在告诉他去哪里，他在追赶，那很有趣。所以它让网站感觉不那么慢了，然后还有这些问题，比如我是点击拖动吗？导航 3D 空间的控制是什么？你知道，我缩放吗？我把那些反转了一段时间。比如我可以旋转屏幕吗？它是自由形式吗？是第一人称吗？是第三人称吗？这让我相当欣赏游戏设计师，因为有很多东西从平面界面设计师的角度来看是不直观的。在导航 3D 空间方面，我有很多事情要做。比如如果你在看一栋建筑的后墙，如果你旋转相机，R 代表旋转，我展示建筑的后墙。但如果然后我有前墙，里面有一个门口，那么你看不到门口。所以我必须稍微展示门口，这样你知道如何离开建筑。必须有这些像悬停时的强调高亮，这样你知道什么是可点击的，因为不是所有东西都是可点击的。所以我有一个像幽灵般的效果，随着芯片出现，这样你知道你在点击什么，这就像所有不同的产品设计相邻的问题，我本来会在其他地方解决，但在 3D 空间中如此不同。我是否让你知道如何爬梯子，或者我是否让你直接点击那里，他就知道如何爬上蜿蜒的梯子？这些是奇怪的问题，因为如果我在第三人称，我旋转这个，喜欢这个交互。如果我旋转这个，你现在仍然可以导航到那个空间。那是我有的同一个瓷砖，但现在在不同的相机视口中，我必须单独导航你。这就像一件奇怪的事情，现在我必须旋转相机。如果你在某个方向移动一定时间，我必须旋转它。这很多。这很多。我见过其他人。

turns.en: It's a lot. And then there's the like the whole like I had to build onboarding for my portfolio. Like there was a weird moment for a while where I was basically saying like, okay, when you when you come to the portfolio, I'll teach you how to play the game. And you had to like do four or five steps in order to use it. And I sent that to quite a few people and they're like, I don't get it. I don't want to do that. Why do I have to click around? Like, is this the game? This feels weird. And then I finally got rid of it. And yeah, it was weird to have be doing user testing on my portfolio, but I had to.
turns.zh: 这很多。然后还有整个像我必须为我的作品集构建入门引导。有一段时间有一个奇怪的时刻，我基本上在说，好吧，当你来到作品集时，我会教你如何玩这个游戏。你必须做四五个步骤才能使用它。我把它发给很多人，他们说，我不明白。我不想那样做。为什么我必须点击？这是游戏吗？这感觉奇怪。然后我终于摆脱了它。是的，对我的作品集进行用户测试很奇怪，但我必须这样做。

turns.en: Okay. I have a question. How much of this is just the raw models acting on the ingenuity of your ideas versus where did it take like a lot of effort to push past what like Claude's going to give you out of the box because very few people I would imagine watching this have built something even remotely close and and I have no idea frankly like I'm every day I'm impressed by like what the models are able to do out of the box for me. I have no idea what is possible here. So like what maybe is easier than you expected versus what is like where you had to put a bunch of reps and iterations in that maybe you didn't expect like help people understand the role that the models are able to play in helping you create something like this.
turns.zh: 好的。我有个问题。这其中有多少只是原始模型作用于你想法的独创性，而哪里需要大量努力才能突破 Claude 开箱即用的能力，因为我想象观看这个的很少有人构建过哪怕接近的东西，坦率地说我也不知道，我每天都对模型能为我开箱即用做的事情印象深刻。我不知道这里什么是可能的。所以也许什么比你预期的更容易，而哪里你必须投入大量重复和迭代，也许你没想到，帮助人们理解模型在帮助你创造这样的东西时能扮演的角色。

turns.en: Yeah, it was really good at hooking up controls to like cameras and making sure that things worked. Like when I said, oh, when I go in the building, collapse or open the panel for it. Like that kind of stuff. And when I leave, add a delay a certain amount of time and make it close. Like it's really good at that kind of stuff. It was really good at generating the assets. Very good. Like this office space in here. I gave it four or five photos of my office and my, you know, my old house in Nashville and like my 3D printer and it designed all this kind of stuff for me. Like I was like, oh, put a table in there and some lighting and it did it.
turns.zh: 是的，它非常擅长将控制连接到相机，并确保事情正常工作。比如当我说，哦，当我进入建筑时，折叠或打开它的面板。那种东西。当我离开时，添加一定时间的延迟并让它关闭。它非常擅长那种东西。它非常擅长生成资产。非常好。比如这里的这个办公空间。我给了它四五张我办公室的照片，还有我，你知道，我在纳什维尔的老房子，还有我的 3D 打印机，它为我设计了所有这些。就像我说，哦，在那里放一张桌子和一些灯光，它就做了。

turns.en: Quick question on that front actually because you did such a good job of having all of the different assets and visuals be really really cohesive. Anything that you had to intentionally do in order to maintain this aesthetic. So when Claude is just like spitting things out, they all look very similar and well put together.
turns.zh: 实际上关于这一点快速问一下，因为你做得非常好，让所有不同的资产和视觉效果非常非常连贯。你有没有必须有意做些什么来维持这种美学。所以当 Claude 只是吐出东西时，它们看起来都非常相似且组合得很好。

turns.en: Well, so I wasn't starting this project from scratch. It's really interesting. I don't think that I would have been able to build this had I not built the game that I was building, Pilgrimage. Because in Pilgrimage, I had to establish that consistent style. Like in here, I had to work on the walk mechanics. That took a long time to get the models to be working and also like cohesive generation of the buildings in this game. All that kind of stuff.
turns.zh: 嗯，所以我并不是从零开始这个项目。这真的很有趣。我认为如果我没有构建我正在构建的游戏 Pilgrimage，我就无法构建这个。因为在 Pilgrimage 中，我必须建立那种一致的风格。比如在这里，我必须研究行走机制。那花了很长时间才让模型工作，还有像这个游戏中建筑的连贯生成。所有那种东西。

turns.en: Are these sprites?
turns.zh: 这些是精灵图吗？

turns.en: No. Well, yes. No, the buildings are not sprites. The buildings are 3JS assets and I've got a shader on top of it. Why are these so small? I need to fix that.
turns.zh: 不。嗯，是的。不，建筑不是精灵图。建筑是 3JS 资产，我在上面有一个着色器。为什么这些这么小？我需要修复那个。

turns.en: But the buildings are not just drag them to make them bigger. The buildings are not sprites. The characters are, but the characters are not a sprite until they are rendered as a sprite. But I had all this background of, okay, I spent a mountain of time in Pilgrimage, about a month, working on a consistent visual style: the saturation of colors, how I want things to have rough edges, how I have the accents, the borders, all that kind of stuff in this game. Just for fun. And I learned a ton about this. And then when I started my portfolio and I realized I wanted to go in the 3D direction, I was basically like, just take all the styling I've done there and put it here. Like just the way that I told you to create the assets there with varying textures and the outside faces are selectable and there's interiors and all that kind of stuff. Just do it here. I think there's even a prompt I have in here where it was basically like, don't fork this repo but kind of fork it to make this work because that's what I had to do. I had to bring in the camera controls, the performance optimizations, and all that kind of stuff into this game in order for it to work well, but I did the rendering in my portfolio completely differently from the one in the game.
turns.zh: 但建筑不是直接拖拽就能放大的。建筑不是精灵图，角色是精灵图，但角色在被渲染成精灵图之前也不是精灵图。但我有所有这些背景，好吧，我在 Pilgrimage 上花了大量时间，大约一个月，研究一致的视觉风格：颜色的饱和度、如何让东西有粗糙的边缘、如何在这个游戏里加入强调、边框等等。只是为了好玩。我学到了很多。然后当我开始做作品集，意识到我想走 3D 方向时，我基本上就是，把我在那里做的所有样式都搬到这里。就像我告诉你在那里创建资产的方式，用不同的纹理，外表面可选，有内部结构等等。就在这里做。我甚至有一个提示词，基本上是说，不要 fork 这个仓库，但为了让它工作，还是得 fork 一下，因为我不得不这样做。我不得不把相机控制、性能优化等等带入这个游戏，才能让它运行良好，但我在作品集里的渲染方式和游戏里的完全不同。

turns.en: I think there's a question I have around how do you want to position yourself? Like, what's the feeling that you want somebody to even have when they come here? Because I know there's somebody watching this and they're like, "This is really cool. Should I do a game? Is this even makes sense for me to go down this type of path?"
turns.zh: 我想问一个关于你想如何定位自己的问题。比如，你希望别人来到这里时有什么感觉？因为我知道有观众在看这个，他们会想：“这真的很酷。我应该做个游戏吗？走这条路对我来说合理吗？”

turns.en: Yeah. I had some people who looked at this and like, "Are you a game designer now?" I was like, "Oh, I'm not a game designer." The representation I want someone to have is this person just wants to have fun. Like literally this is totally rid— Look at this. Look at this. Welcome to Tom Jungle. Like that is rid— I would never have this thing lying around. But I tool tip.
turns.zh: 是的。有些人看了这个说：“你现在是游戏设计师了？”我说：“哦，我不是游戏设计师。”我希望给人的印象是，这个人只是想玩得开心。真的，这完全荒诞——看看这个。看看这个。“欢迎来到 Tom Jungle”。这太荒诞了——我永远不会把这种东西摆在那里。但我有工具提示。

turns.en: Yeah. I love I kind of love propaganda posters. Like I had some old propaganda posters when I was in college hang up on my walls because I think they're so visually striking, but they're also just like World War II propaganda from everyone is ridiculous. And so I was like, well, I want to make my own propaganda poster for Welcome to Tom Johnville. It's kind of like this idealic city of Boomer Town or something like that. Wouldn't that be fun? And it's in a font that I would never use. Like it's just I just want someone to be able to come here and say not like, "Oh, should I do this for myself?" But what do you have that is built off of the things that you've worked on? What do you have that communicates clearly? Like are you a minimalist or like perfect typography or do you have some kind of like crazy hobby that is outside of this? If you're doing an agency model, you'd have to do things a little bit differently. But if you're doing this just for like someone can click on my link and know who I am, then you know, just have fun with it because there's no limitations on what the models are capable of or what you can do with them. It's just insane how much is possible.
turns.zh: 是的。我喜欢——我有点喜欢宣传海报。我大学时墙上挂过一些老宣传海报，因为我觉得它们视觉冲击力很强，但它们也就是二战宣传，来自每个人都荒谬。所以我想，好吧，我想为“欢迎来到 Tom Johnville”做我自己的宣传海报。它有点像 Boomer Town 这种理想城市之类的。那不好玩吗？而且用的字体是我永远不会用的。就像我只是希望别人来到这里时，不是想说“哦，我应该为自己做这个吗？”而是你有什么是基于你做过的东西构建的？你有什么能清晰传达的？比如你是极简主义者还是完美排版，或者你有什么疯狂的业余爱好？如果你做代理模式，你得做得有点不同。但如果你只是为了让别人点我的链接就知道我是谁，那就玩得开心点，因为模型的能力没有限制，你能用它们做什么也没有限制。可能性多得疯狂。

turns.en: Well, that's my reaction actually. Like, I see this and I'm like, Tom is somebody who just has a blatant disregard of previous limitations and what it meant to be a designer even where it's like you can tell you're just somebody that's you're just pushing as far as you can possibly go in every direction simultaneously. It's hard to pull off though, but I mean, you obviously did it.
turns.zh: 嗯，这其实是我的反应。我看到这个就想，Tom 是一个公然无视先前限制和设计师意义的人，甚至你能看出你就是一个同时向各个方向尽可能推进的人。这很难做到，但我的意思是，你显然做到了。

turns.en: Not to toot my own horn, but I've realized this is something when a new tool comes out in the market, my first reaction is like let's break it. Let's see how far I can creatively go with this and I have hit limits with this but 3JS is kind of the thing that holds me back a little bit the performance in the browser and all that but when Webflow first came out I was using it and man I was pushing that pretty hard and breaking and finding the limits and just finding the edges of like where can I be creative what is the space I live and not saying like I want to break the tool it's more like well if I can do X then I can do Y then I can do Z and then you hit the wall like okay there's the end and then I did the same thing when Figma was released I was like, "Wow, I can do everything in the browser now. I can have these kind of crazy experiments and started reaching the edges of what that tool was capable of." And like did some weird hacks and workarounds that I'm still kind of shocked at to this day that I was able to get working in the browser. But it's been fun, I think, whenever there's a new tool in the space to just say like what's the thing that I can do that breaks it? Framer, Claude, insert tool here. What can I do and what's the most I can do in this tool to not constrain my creativity?
turns.zh: 不是自夸，但我意识到，当市场上有新工具出现时，我的第一反应就是，让我们突破它。看看我在创意上能走多远，我确实遇到过限制，但 3JS 是有点阻碍我的东西，浏览器里的性能等等，但当 Webflow 刚出来时，我在用它，天哪，我把它推得很狠，突破并找到极限，找到我能有创意的边缘，我生活的空间，不是说我想破坏工具，而是说如果我能做 X，就能做 Y，然后做 Z，然后你撞墙了，好吧，到头了。然后 Figma 发布时我也做了同样的事，我想：“哇，我现在可以在浏览器里做一切了。我可以做这些疯狂的实验，并开始触及那个工具能力的边缘。”还做了一些奇怪的 hack 和变通方法，至今我仍对自己能在浏览器里搞定感到震惊。但我觉得很有趣，每当这个领域有新工具时，就说我能做什么来突破它？Framer、Claude，插入任何工具。我能做什么，在这个工具里我能做的最大程度是什么，以不限制我的创造力？

turns.en: I mean I think that experimentation at least in my experience has produced a lot of the learning that has like you know accelerated different parts or different chapters of my career. I think it's easy to look at this as maybe a skeptic and be like this is so far disconnected from digital products that you would actually make for work or anything and like does this even translate to anything? Do any of these learnings carry over to you know maybe other you know work or other things that you're making or even at a high level how you work with the models like talk to me about that for a little bit.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，至少在我的经验中，这种实验产生了很多学习，加速了我职业生涯的不同部分或不同篇章。我觉得很容易以怀疑者的眼光看这个，说这与你实际为工作做的数字产品太脱节了，这甚至能转化为什么吗？这些学习中有任何能带到其他工作或其他你正在做的东西中吗，或者甚至在高层次上你如何与模型合作，跟我谈谈这个。

turns.en: If I was speaking to Tom who hadn't built this before I built this I'd be like there's not a lot of overlap here like game design this kind of design 3D spaces is not like a lot is very different skill to flux and now having done this there is a massive amount of overlap. The way that you have to think about the 3D spaces is different, but it's also like maybe I was designing something spatial like something for like 3D glasses or something like that. I would have to think about occlusion and I would have to think about performance or rendering or viewport or like how do I treat the camera as an entity kind of like how I would treat the cursor or the device or the user all those types of things. Like there's a lot of overlap here. It's just a different way of thinking about it. And the overlap with other projects is dramatic. Like like I said, the Pilgrimage game that I was building led to this. Like this asset in here is from that game. So are a lot of the trees and so are a lot of the textures and stuff like that. These rabbits are even from the game. Like I didn't generate those for this. I pulled them in from that game.
turns.zh: 如果我在做这个之前跟那个还没做过这个的 Tom 说话，我会说这里重叠不多，游戏设计、这种 3D 空间设计，不是很多，是与 Flux 非常不同的技能，但现在做了这个之后，有大量的重叠。你必须以不同方式思考 3D 空间，但也像是我在设计空间性的东西，比如为 3D 眼镜设计之类的。我不得不考虑遮挡，考虑性能或渲染或视口，或者如何把相机当作一个实体，就像我对待光标或设备或用户那样。这里有很多重叠。只是不同的思考方式。与其他项目的重叠是巨大的。就像我说的，我在做的 Pilgrimage 游戏导致了这个。这里的这个资产来自那个游戏。很多树也是，很多纹理之类的也是。这些兔子甚至来自那个游戏。我不是为这个生成的。我从那个游戏里拉过来的。

turns.en: But like I had a very rudimentary set of tools that I brought into this, and I was able to make something that just took those building pieces and made something completely novel. There's very little overlap between the two now. But I started with that rough set of ingredients. Now, I've taken the stuff I've learned here and I've worked on this other thing that I've built—this app for myself. So this one is a legitimate potential business. It's called White Knuckle. I built this camper rig in the game because I was like, well, what better way to represent this? I wanted to see if I could generate it. What are the models capable of? Can they really generate this realistic working camper that folds the slides and puts down the porch and lowers the beds and stuff like that? This was more like me saying, what can I do or what can't I do? And then the other day we were talking about where we want to go this next month in California, and I want to go to Yosemite in California, and there's this little strip of road on California Highway 120. It goes between the Central Valley and the lower foothills going up into the mountains. My camper nav says that I can make that route. And I looked at it on a map and I was like, there is no way I can make that route. There may not be clearances, there may not be length restrictions or anything like that, but I'm looking at this thing and I'm like, I don't want to drive this. And that's the only way you can get to the only campground that's near Yosemite for us. I was like, okay, so it's either I take that road and take someone else's word for it, or I don't go. And so I was like, well, maybe I could bring this model in and simulate it. So I built a very rough idea. I just told Claude, put it on a map, use 3D data, and drive it and see how it works. And so it generated this. This was the one shot and it's bad. It's very bad, but it was a proof of concept. I was like, wow, that's really interesting. I can see my rig on the road. It added all these annotations for where I might go over the lane, all that kind of stuff. And so then I shared this initial thing in one of the Facebook groups for the campers that I drive. And other people were like, oh, can I use this? Please build this. I want to build it. I would use this all the time. And they're like, this is a significant problem. And so over the last four weeks, I've now been building this based off of this model and this truck. Where's the truck in the game? There's my truck. This truck is the base model for the game and this camper. And I built an entire app based off of those two little building blocks. If I had not done this ridiculous thing in my portfolio, I wouldn't have this crazy app that now generates realistic turning radiuses for campers. Because this is where things get weird. You think in a car mindset—how do you actually turn a corner? I think in terms of: I have 46 feet behind me, my back tires. I have to take this route right here and then the camper might miss that corner. And that's the way you have to come about driving these routes. And then there's also entries to tunnels. And I'm like, well, okay, I might hit on the right side of that tunnel but I'll be fine in the center part. How do I know when I have a tunnel if it says I'm clear or not? What are the actual dimensions of the tunnel approach? Which is a crazy thing to know about, but I have to know that because if I mess up, I could literally destroy my house.
turns.zh: 但我当时只有一套非常基础的工具，我能够用这些构建模块做出完全新颖的东西。现在两者之间几乎没有重叠。但我从这套粗略的素材开始。现在，我把在这里学到的东西用在了我构建的另一个东西上——这个我自己开发的应用。所以这个是一个合法的潜在业务。它叫 White Knuckle。我在游戏里构建了这个露营车组合，因为我想，还有什么更好的方式来表示这个呢？我想看看我能不能生成它。模型能做什么？它们真的能生成这个逼真的、能折叠滑梯、放下门廊、降下床铺等等的工作露营车吗？这更像是我在问自己，我能做什么或不能做什么？然后前几天我们在讨论下个月在加州想去哪里，我想去加州的优胜美地，加州 120 号公路上有一小段路。它穿过中央谷地和低矮丘陵，向上进入山区。我的露营车导航说我可以走那条路线。我在地图上看了看，我说我绝对走不了那条路线。可能没有净空限制，可能没有长度限制之类的，但我看着这个东西，我说我不想开这条路。而那是我们到达优胜美地附近唯一露营地的唯一方式。我说，好吧，要么我走那条路并相信别人的话，要么我就不去。所以我想，也许我可以把这个模型带进来模拟一下。所以我构建了一个非常粗略的想法。我告诉 Claude，把它放到地图上，使用 3D 数据，然后驾驶它看看效果如何。于是它生成了这个。这是第一次尝试，很糟糕。非常糟糕，但这是一个概念验证。我说，哇，这真的很有趣。我可以在路上看到我的车。它添加了所有这些注释，比如我可能越过车道的地方，诸如此类。然后我把这个初始版本分享到了我驾驶的露营车的一个 Facebook 群里。其他人说，哦，我能用这个吗？请构建这个。我想构建它。我会一直用这个。他们说，这是一个重要的问题。所以在过去的四周里，我一直在基于这个模型和这辆卡车构建这个。游戏里的卡车在哪里？这是我的卡车。这辆卡车是游戏的基础模型，还有这个露营车。我基于这两个小构建块构建了一个完整的应用。如果我没有在我的作品集里做这件荒谬的事，我就不会有这个疯狂的应用，它现在能为露营车生成逼真的转弯半径。因为这就是事情变得奇怪的地方。你以汽车的思维思考——你实际上如何转弯？我考虑的是：我后面有 46 英尺，我的后轮胎。我必须走这条路线，然后露营车可能会错过那个弯。这就是你驾驶这些路线的方式。还有隧道的入口。我想，好吧，我可能会撞到隧道的右侧，但在中间部分我会没事的。我怎么知道隧道是否说我可以通过？隧道入口的实际尺寸是多少？这是一个疯狂的知识点，但我必须知道，因为如果我搞砸了，我可能会毁了我的房子。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And everyone is going through this right now. When you're driving around, when you see big rigs on the road, we're all dealing with this. Do I fit?
turns.zh: 现在每个人都在经历这个。当你开车到处走，当你在路上看到大型卡车时，我们都在处理这个问题。我能不能通过？

turns.en: This is so cool. This is a world that I have never considered.
turns.zh: 这太酷了。这是我从未考虑过的世界。

turns.en: And I'm just working with Claude on this. And it's a remarkable amount of depth that I've now found myself in working on this in the evenings. I'll just prompt it and send it off and see what happens in the morning when I come up. And now I've suddenly created a full world simulated generator with interchanges and intersections and turn-by-turn guidance. And I'm dealing with, okay, so how do I plot interchanges in New York City where things are dramatically different? How do I have variable textures for different trees? And how do I do bridges? How do I do procedurally generated bridges? Because there's a whole bunch of iconic bridges. And then there's also, oh no, parking lots. I got to generate parking lots. How do I do that? And now I'm in the world where I also have to generate the truck because the pin length is different for every truck. And then the hitch you're using for the truck is different because that changes the turning dynamics. And there's also, where are my brakes going to overheat? So I have to have ambient temperature and what time of year you're driving and all this weird stuff that every single one of these things would be—two years ago mindset would be, oh, this is a blocker. We can't do this.
turns.zh: 而我只是在和 Claude 一起做这个。我现在发现自己晚上都在研究这个，深度惊人。我只需提示它并发送出去，然后早上起来看看发生了什么。现在我突然创建了一个完整的世界模拟生成器，带有立交桥、交叉路口和逐向导航。我在处理，好吧，那么我如何在纽约市绘制立交桥，那里情况截然不同？我如何为不同的树木设置不同的纹理？我如何做桥梁？我如何程序化生成桥梁？因为有很多标志性桥梁。然后还有，哦不，停车场。我得生成停车场。我怎么做？现在我还得生成卡车，因为每辆卡车的轴距长度不同。然后你使用的卡车挂钩也不同，因为那会改变转弯动力学。还有我的刹车会在哪里过热？所以我必须有环境温度和你在什么季节驾驶，以及所有这些奇怪的东西，每一件事在两年前的心态都会是，哦，这是一个障碍。我们做不到。

turns.en: Yeah, there's no way.
turns.zh: 是的，不可能。

turns.en: Well, not only that, but I'm looking at this and I'm like, two years ago, I wouldn't even have known where I could have possibly inserted myself into a project like this, even if I wanted to. It's like how much static design is even there? There's a little bits of UI where I'm not going to be the one that's going to be custom drawing the 3D assets. That's not my skill set. Everything else is just raw engineering, man. You know?
turns.zh: 嗯，不仅如此，我看着这个，我想，两年前，我甚至不知道我可能在哪里插入这样一个项目，即使我想。有多少静态设计在那里？有一点点 UI，我不会是那个自定义绘制 3D 资产的人。那不是我的技能。其他一切都是纯粹的工程，伙计。你知道吗？

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. It's also like comparing all the different data sets together.
turns.zh: 是的。是的。这也像是把所有不同的数据集比较在一起。

turns.en: Yeah. And like trying to make custom tooling and like because it's not just one data set. There's actually like 13 different data sets and it varies by state. There's open source LAR data sets that are available in California or Georgia but not New York. There's all this different stuff that I have to pour through to find the most accurate data and also do it in a way that's like I can afford because these data sets are expensive. And so I'm having to derive all this kind of stuff, but once you get it, once you get the accurate satellite imagery, you can actually do something like this, which is something I set up this morning. My wife is like, oh, we're going to book a campground. We want a lot of shade because the one side of the camper has awnings on it.
turns.zh: 是的。而且就像尝试制作自定义工具，因为不仅仅是一个数据集。实际上有 13 个不同的数据集，而且因州而异。有开源的 LAR 数据集在加州或乔治亚州可用，但在纽约不可用。我必须梳理所有这些不同的东西来找到最准确的数据，并且以我能负担的方式来做，因为这些数据集很昂贵。所以我不得不推导所有这些，但一旦你得到它，一旦你得到准确的卫星图像，你实际上可以做这样的事情，这是我今天早上设置的。我妻子说，哦，我们要预订一个露营地。我们想要很多阴凉，因为露营车的一侧有遮阳篷。

turns.en: We've parked places for a while and we don't get any shade because the sun is the wrong way. And I was like, "Well, I could build that." So now I have this whole thing that literally—I know from a satellite image I can generate a realistic model of the campground, and I can select a campsite, see if I fit, and also time of day based off of what year.
turns.zh: 我们曾在一些地方停过房车，但一直晒不到阴凉，因为太阳方向不对。我就想：“嗯，我可以做一个工具。”所以现在我有这么一套东西：只要有一张卫星图像，我就能生成营地的逼真模型，我可以选择营地，看看我的房车能不能停进去，还能根据年份查看一天中不同时间的阴影情况。

turns.en: Unbelievable. Wow.
turns.zh: 难以置信。哇。

turns.en: Which is—I cannot tell you how valuable this is as a camper because it's not just the shade. It's also now I have a 3D model potentially of a campground. I can know if I fit in the campground. That's a big deal. There are so many campgrounds where you show up and you're like, "I don't fit down this road" or "this spot said it was too big or too small." Will I actually fit? These things are really valuable for someone who has a significant amount invested in the thing that you're driving. And now I can just build it. I can just—you know why not? I've got all this kind of crazy stuff that I'm able to spin up. And it all started because of this weird idea of "what if I put my camper in my portfolio?" It's ridiculous. But these just lead into each other. You start realizing if I can do that with one tool, I can bring that over and I can solve it in another tool, and they just beget new ideas. It's almost like—I used to do a little bit of woodworking and you would buy a tool. I would buy a tool and I'd be like, "I'm not going to use that for anything else. I just need this for this one thing and I can't justify it." You know, it's just—but I have to need—I have to buy this tool for this one situation. And you buy it and you put it in your garage and then like a week later you're like, "Oh, I have that tool. I can do that thing. I can solve that problem now because I have the tool that I never thought of it before and now I can solve that problem." And I feel like that's where we are now where I have so many different pieces that I can just mush together, that I can create my own tools or bring pieces from a portfolio to a product that I need. And it's just wild what you can do now.
turns.zh: 这——我无法告诉你这对一个露营者来说有多大的价值，因为不仅仅是阴凉。现在我还可能拥有营地的 3D 模型。我能知道我的房车能不能停进营地。这很重要。有很多营地，你到了那里才发现“这条路我过不去”或者“这个位置标着太大或太小”。我到底能不能停进去？对于在驾驶的车辆上投入了大量资金的人来说，这些东西真的很有价值。现在我可以直接构建它。我可以——你知道，为什么不呢？我有所有这些疯狂的东西可以快速做出来。而这一切都始于一个奇怪的想法：“如果我把我的房车放进作品集里会怎样？”这很荒谬。但这些想法会相互引导。你开始意识到，如果我能用一个工具做到那件事，我就可以把它带到另一个工具里解决问题，它们会催生新的想法。这几乎就像——我以前做过一点木工，你会买一个工具。我会买一个工具，然后想：“我不会用它做别的。我只是为了这一件事需要它，我无法证明买它是合理的。”你知道，只是——但我必须需要——我必须为这一种情况买这个工具。你买了它，把它放在车库里，然后一周后你会想：“哦，我有那个工具。我可以做那件事。我现在可以解决那个问题了，因为我有那个工具，我以前从未想过，现在我可以解决那个问题了。”我觉得我们现在就处于这样的阶段：我有这么多不同的部件，可以随意组合，我可以创建自己的工具，或者把作品集中的部件带到一个我需要的产品中。你现在能做的事情真是太疯狂了。

turns.en: Okay. You brought up like the two year ago timeline. I feel like a lot of designers, myself included, you know, there's been this almost like stretching yourself a little bit. Like how far out of the comfort zone can you go? How far down some of these paths can you go? This is the farthest I think maybe I've ever seen anybody go personally. Like in terms of who I would have considered like, yeah, that's a designer. You know, a lot of designers making custom tools. I've never seen anything like this. This is crazy stuff, right? Like this is heavy lifting custom tools. And honestly, even the product itself, economically, it couldn't exist 2 years ago. The opportunity is too small and the lift is too high where like this product, you actually are the first person maybe on planet Earth that's ever had the ability, motive, time, like every single piece needs to come together in order to make something like this. And so if you think about like how far you're stretching yourself, dude, you're like out here, man, where I would imagine it how can you go back, you know? Like there's like there's no what role if you wanted to even get hired for this kind of thing like what what is this you know like I don't know are you wrestling with that at all like this is crazy stuff what you're sharing.
turns.zh: 好。你提到了两年前的时间线。我觉得很多设计师，包括我自己，你知道，几乎都有这种稍微拉伸自己的感觉。你能走出舒适区多远？你能在这些路径上走多远？这可能是我个人见过的最远的了。就我认为“对，那是个设计师”的人而言。你知道，很多设计师在做自定义工具。我从未见过这样的东西。这很疯狂，对吧？这就像是重型起重般的自定义工具。老实说，甚至产品本身，在经济上，两年前也不可能存在。机会太小，而难度太高，这个产品，你实际上可能是地球上第一个有能力、有动机、有时间的人，每一个环节都需要结合在一起才能做出这样的东西。所以如果你想想你拉伸自己的程度，老兄，你就像在这里，伙计，我想象中，你怎么能回去呢，你知道？就像没有——如果你想甚至被雇佣来做这种事，角色是什么？这到底是什么？你知道，我不知道，你对此有纠结吗？你分享的东西太疯狂了。

ts.sec: Identity and Decisions as a Designer

turns.en: No, I'm—I'm so much—I'm wrestling with it because it also feels like as a designer before I was so tied into what I would output, like the decisions I made, the visual representation of the ideas that I had on the canvas. Not that I still—like I still use canvas tools and all that kind of stuff. And I'm not trying to like make this a hot button issue like that, but I was so—I was so tied into "I can say that I did work because I can see the decisions."
turns.zh: 不，我——我非常——我在纠结，因为这也感觉像是，作为一名设计师，以前我如此紧密地与我的输出绑定，比如我做的决定、我在画布上对想法的视觉呈现。并不是说我仍然——我仍然使用画布工具之类的。我不是想把这变成一个热点问题，但我如此——我如此紧密地绑定于“我可以说我做了工作，因为我能看到决定”。

turns.en: And I realized lately like working in this way I lost the ability to showcase all these decisions and I'm like grateful that I get a chance to go on this podcast now cuz I—I get my portfolio I could talk about it for a very long time and not because of the like oh look at this but the decisions—the decisions that were there and I've lost that ability to articulate the decisions that were made. The way that I navigated the waters, the way that I felt as a designer was kind of tied into my—my who am I? What role am I? How do I live within an organization? What can I do? What are the boundaries? I—oh I don't do sales or I don't do media. I don't do—don't do support or whatever it is. I've lost the ability to kind of like anchor myself on that output. And what I've realized now is like the series of prompts that I'm doing are kind of like the rough stumbling around on the canvas, like that they're kind of like the articulation of the decisions that I have. Like if you look at this white knuckle case study, it's—it's not a case study. I'm not like saying, "Oh, here's a canvas." It's just every single prompt that I used along the way as—
turns.zh: 我最近意识到，以这种方式工作，我失去了展示所有这些决定的能力，我很感激现在有机会上这个播客，因为——我有了我的作品集，我可以谈论它很长时间，不是因为“哦看这个”，而是因为决定——那些决定，我失去了阐述所做决定的能力。我 navigating 水域的方式，我作为设计师的感受，某种程度上与我的——我是谁？我是什么角色？我如何在组织中生存？我能做什么？边界是什么？我——哦，我不做销售，或者我不做媒体。我不做——不做支持或 whatever。我失去了将自己锚定在输出上的能力。我现在意识到的是，我做的一系列提示词就像在画布上粗略地摸索，就像它们是我所拥有决定的阐述。就像如果你看这个 white knuckle 案例研究，它——它不是案例研究。我不是在说“哦，这里有一个画布。”它只是我沿途使用的每一个提示词，作为——

turns.en: I just made that connection that you're— Oh, that's cool. Interesting.
turns.zh: 我刚建立了那个联系，你——哦，那很酷。有趣。

turns.en: Yeah. So, this is like me saying, "Hey, I realized like this—this is actually something I'm making a skill for. I'm calling it Gretle because I've realized in working I've lost my breadcrumbs."
turns.zh: 是的。所以，这就像我在说：“嘿，我意识到这——这实际上是我正在为之打造一项技能的东西。我把它叫做 Gretle，因为我意识到在工作中我丢失了我的面包屑。”

turns.en: Oh, dude, that's so good. I felt this recently. It's so good. There's one question that I can't stop asking myself. What if companies applied to talk to you rather than the other way around? And that question is the foundation for the all-new Dive Talent Network. And it's working. Like right now, I'm helping many of the most exciting startups that I know to hire the designers and builders who listen to this show. So, if you're curious what might be out there and maybe you want to get on my list, or maybe you're even looking for your next design hire, head to dive.comclub/talent to join today.
turns.zh: 哦，老兄，那太好了。我最近也有这种感觉。太好了。有一个问题我忍不住问自己。如果公司申请和你交谈，而不是反过来，会怎样？这个问题是全新的 Dive Talent Network 的基础。而且它正在起作用。就像现在，我正在帮助我认识的许多最令人兴奋的初创公司雇佣收听这个节目的设计师和构建者。所以，如果你好奇外面可能有什么，也许你想加入我的名单，或者你甚至正在寻找你的下一个设计雇员，请访问 dive.comclub/talent 今天就加入。

turns.en: I went into a discussion a little while ago with something that I like had built and I coded all myself over a series of months and there's so much. It was something that I like spent poured myself into and I had to articulate the design decisions I had along the way and I had nothing.
turns.zh: 不久前，我参与了一个讨论，关于我构建的东西，我花了几个月时间自己编码，有很多。那是我倾注心血的东西，我不得不阐述我沿途所做的设计决定，而我什么都没有。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: I had the final version of the product and I had the vision of it, and I was clicking around in the product, using the real thing. It's crazy that I was able to build it, but I had nothing to say. When people were asking, 'Show me, did you explore this in the past?' I'd say, 'Yeah, it's over here on this canvas. This is where I decided to use this icon, or this is where I tried 30 different versions of this.'
turns.zh: 我有了产品的最终版本，也有了它的愿景，我在产品里点来点去，用的是真实的东西。我能把它做出来真是太疯狂了，但我却没什么可说的。当人们问‘给我看看，你过去探索过这个吗？’我会说‘是的，在这块画布上。这是我决定用这个图标的地方，或者这是我尝试了 30 个不同版本的地方。’

turns.en: And I have that when I tell my agent, 'Try 10 versions of this.' I've seen you say this: 'Make 10 different better versions of this.' But I've lost my articulation of those. Maybe it's like, 'Okay, yeah, here's 10 versions and I picked one,' but I don't have that visually where I can see, 'Here's where I picked one.'
turns.zh: 当我告诉我的智能体‘试试这个的 10 个版本’时，我有这种感觉。我见过你说‘做 10 个不同的更好的版本’。但我已经失去了对这些的清晰表达。也许就像‘好吧，是的，这里有 10 个版本，我选了一个’，但我没有那种视觉上的东西，让我能看到‘这是我选了一个的地方’。

turns.en: So what I did here with these case studies is it's literally the sloppy prompt that was around this image that shows some kind of rough approximation of what I was thinking when I was going back there. So if someone was ever to be like, 'Hey, when did you decide to do your map in this certain style?' I could be like, 'Right here, that's the prompt I sent,' or something like that. It's still messy, but it's like I have now a path. I have my breadcrumbs that I can follow back.
turns.zh: 所以我在这里对这些案例研究所做的，实际上就是围绕这张图像的草率提示词，它展示了我当时在想什么的某种粗略近似。所以如果有人问‘嘿，你什么时候决定用这种风格做你的地图？’我可以像‘就在这里，那就是我发送的提示词’之类的。它仍然很乱，但就像我现在有了一条路径。我有我可以回溯的面包屑。

turns.en: And I can still—as soon as I did this, I was like, 'Oh, I'm still a designer.' It was like I was missing the decisions that I had made along the way, and now I'm going to be working like this fully. I've got a skill set up where it will now dump any vibecoded tool that I do. It will start dumping this log of decisions, this prompt, into something that I can reference, and I can also share that with someone else so that they can feed it into their models as context, like, 'Okay, well, maybe this is—I need to hand it off to you.'
turns.zh: 而且我仍然可以——我一这样做，我就想‘哦，我还是个设计师。’就像我丢失了一路上所做的决定，现在我要完全这样工作了。我已经设置了一个技能，它现在会把我做的任何 vibecoded 工具都倾倒出来。它会开始把这份决策日志、这个提示词倾倒到我可以参考的东西里，我也可以把它分享给别人，这样他们就可以把它作为上下文输入到他们的模型中，就像‘好吧，也许这是——我需要把它交给你。’

turns.en: It can go in this way. And yeah, I feel like there's a really interesting idea there because we've lost that articulation, we've lost that identity of a designer that was so tied to the canvas tools, and design decisions are still happening, they're still happening.
turns.zh: 它可以这样进去。是的，我觉得那里有一个非常有趣的想法，因为我们失去了那种清晰表达，我们失去了设计师的身份，那种与画布工具紧密相连的身份，而设计决策仍在发生，它们仍在发生。

turns.en: Not only that, but there's a perceived value of the idea that I think humans subconsciously attach to the end output when they can see the amount of work that goes into it. Where some of your best work, especially on White Knuckle, actually might just be you had a really good idea and you just told the agent to run it and then you went to sleep and you woke up and it was done.
turns.zh: 不仅如此，还有一种对想法的感知价值，我认为人类会潜意识地将其附加到最终输出上，当他们能看到投入的工作量时。而你的一些最好的作品，尤其是在 White Knuckle 上，实际上可能只是你有一个非常好的想法，你只是告诉智能体去运行它，然后你去睡觉，醒来时它就完成了。

turns.en: And you lose that perceived quality even though it's a really good idea and you were able to make it happen, which was designing. I was talking about this with my friend the other day where it's like it feels like we have all of potentially the right answers for the geometry tests but we don't have the geometry proofs anymore. Can you build this?
turns.zh: 你失去了那种感知质量，即使这是一个非常好的想法，而且你能够实现它，这就是设计。前几天我和我的朋友谈论这个，感觉就像我们可能拥有几何测试的所有正确答案，但我们不再有几何证明了。你能构建这个吗？

turns.en: Yeah, you can't show your work.
turns.zh: 是的，你不能展示你的工作。

turns.en: Yeah. And I feel like there's a certain level where it's like I don't need to show my work. Like I got the decision, the user test or whatever it was. We don't necessarily need to show what led to it. But then there are certain ideas that you have where you're like that was a good idea and I want to show that I made—like how what went into it.
turns.zh: 是的。我觉得在某种程度上，就像我不需要展示我的工作。比如我得到了决定、用户测试或其他什么。我们不一定需要展示导致它的原因。但然后有些想法，你会觉得那是个好主意，我想展示我做了——比如投入了什么。

turns.en: And let me show you one that I had this morning because I'm sharing this with people on social media. I'm sharing this app and I'm like screen recording on my phone or it's sloppy. All this kind of stuff. I don't like it because it's not the way that I want my app to be presented while I'm developing it. And so I was like, 'Oh, I'll just build a media studio inside of the app.' So I'll generate a scene here. And then it shows me how it works on Instagram reels and then I can give it the camera shots that I want. So I want this to be a side shot. I actually want this to be a road shot for, you know, 10 seconds. And then I can see the output and it'll generate the whole scene for me. Let me start from—let me start over here.
turns.zh: 让我给你看一个我今天早上有的，因为我在社交媒体上与人分享这个。我在分享这个应用，我在手机上录屏，或者它很草率。所有这些。我不喜欢它，因为这不是我在开发时想要展示我的应用的方式。所以我想‘哦，我就在应用里建一个媒体工作室。’所以我在这里生成一个场景。然后它向我展示它在 Instagram reels 上如何运作，然后我可以给它我想要的镜头。所以我想让这个成为侧拍。我实际上想让它成为路拍，你知道，10 秒钟。然后我可以看到输出，它会为我生成整个场景。让我从——让我从这里开始。

turns.en: But I'm like, I can share that on social like that's going to be real.
turns.zh: 但我想，我可以在社交媒体上分享那个，那会是真的。

turns.en: Yeah. And I can see the highlights and all this kind of stuff and it's like—and I didn't build any of this, you know, but I have the prompts that led to the idea and I have the output and now all I have to do is prepare it and I can output this thing and it'll generate it and I have an asset. And like that's the kind of idea where it's like am I a designer now? I'm doing media. You have—you're a founder. You have to promote your work. You have to get it out there. And if you can use these tools to help you better articulate it, then man, it's just like you can do so much more than you used to be able to.
turns.zh: 是的。我可以看到亮点和所有这些，就像——我没有构建任何这些，你知道，但我有导致这个想法的提示词，我有输出，现在我所要做的就是准备它，我可以输出这个东西，它会生成它，我就有了一个资产。就像那种想法，就像我现在是设计师吗？我在做媒体。你有——你是创始人。你必须推广你的工作。你必须把它传播出去。如果你能用这些工具帮助你更好地表达它，那么伙计，就像你能做比以前多得多的事情。

turns.en: I mean, it's like on my portfolio, I have a mirrored version of everything as a static page. So if I want to send someone a case study and I want to feel professional, I have it. I have the game version and I have the pro version, but I can send you either of them. I don't really care. But it depends on what you're looking for. And so like you can now say, 'Well, I want these all to be mirrored and I don't have to worry about a CMS or I don't have to worry about all these issues with limitations of the platform.'
turns.zh: 我的意思是，就像在我的作品集上，我有一个所有东西的镜像版本作为静态页面。所以如果我想发送给某人一个案例研究，并且我想感觉专业，我有它。我有游戏版本，我有专业版本，但我可以发送给你任何一个。我真的不在乎。但这取决于你在寻找什么。所以现在你可以说‘好吧，我想让这些都镜像，我不必担心 CMS，或者我不必担心所有这些平台限制的问题。’

turns.en: Can we hop back into your portfolio and look at some of those prompts? And I know this is like the last thing in the world that I ever want anybody to do is look at my prompts for thousands of people to see. We're not gonna go through them too closely, but it hits on—there's this thing that I'm experiencing and I have genuine—I'm self-conscious about it basically. And I think there's all these questions of like am I a designer? Am I a designer? This is one of the things that's really hitting me where my prompts actually look a lot like your prompts right now. And they started off in the beginning when I'm prompting with AI. It's all about use the right language, be specific, give all the con—you know, I had really dialed in prompts and now some of my best prompts might be like this looks messy over here. turns.en: Like the down and to the right beauty for me was like, 'You know what? I'm going to spend the next 4 hours doing nothing but thinking about this one thing.' I never get that anymore. Ever. turns.en: If I was doing the white-knuckle thing — if I was doing white-knuckle here, you know, and back in the old world — I would know every single scrap of like where this data was coming from, how we're rendering it, I would know the backend structure, I would know, you know, how is this rendering. turns.zh: 如果我还在做那种“硬着头皮死磕”的事——如果我在这里硬着头皮死磕，你知道，回到旧世界——我会知道每一丁点细节，比如这个数据从哪来、我们怎么渲染它，我会知道后端结构，我会知道，你知道，这是怎么渲染的。别太苛刻地评判这个——我想改进的地方很多——但在那里我会知道卫星数据从哪来。我可能参加过谈判企业费率的那个电话，或者我知道有哪些限制。我会知道这些线是怎么画的，知道向量模型的特性，或者如果我是这个产品的一部分，我会知道这个产品的一切。而现在我就像，我并不真的知道数据从哪来。我只是告诉它去找，它找到了，我记不住那叫什么名字。

consensus.en: Designers should show personality in portfolios, not hide behind minimal walls of logos.
consensus.zh: 设计师应在作品集中展现个性，而非躲在极简的标识墙后。

consensus.en: AI models excel at generating assets and wiring controls, but struggle with simplifying UX.
consensus.zh: AI 模型擅长生成素材和连接控件，但难以简化用户体验。

consensus.en: Prompting is a design exercise of noticing what's wrong and iterating, not perfect grammar.
consensus.zh: 提示词是发现错误并迭代的设计练习，而非追求完美语法。

consensus.en: The speed of AI compresses idea-to-output time, enabling focus on bigger picture decisions.
consensus.zh: AI 的速度压缩了从想法到产出的时间，使设计师能聚焦更宏观的决策。

consensus.en: Designers must preserve decision trails (breadcrumbs) to articulate design rationale in AI workflows.
consensus.zh: 设计师必须在 AI 工作流中保留决策轨迹（面包屑），以阐明设计理由。

consensus.en: Experimentation with new tools to find their limits accelerates career learning and creativity.
consensus.zh: 用新工具实验以探索其极限，能加速职业学习与创造力。

contrarian.en: Portfolios should be playful playgrounds, not professional walls of work.
contrarian.zh: 作品集应是好玩的游乐场，而非职业化的作品墙。

contrarian.en: AI is doing the design; designers are just picking and providing taste.
contrarian.zh: AI 在做设计；设计师只是挑选并提供品味。

contrarian.en: Prompt engineering is dead; just say what you want in natural language.
contrarian.zh: 提示词工程已死；只需用自然语言说出你想要什么。

contrarian.en: Losing granular control in AI workflows is acceptable; focus on high-level decisions.
contrarian.zh: 在 AI 工作流中失去细粒度控制是可接受的；应关注高层决策。

contrarian.en: The old canvas iteration process was often a waste of time; AI enables real building.
contrarian.zh: 旧的画布迭代过程常常是浪费时间；AI 让真实构建成为可能。

contrarian.en: Designers should not be precious about prompts; share them openly like Slack messages.
contrarian.zh: 设计师不应吝惜提示词；应像 Slack 消息一样公开分享。
